newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia energy body sets new oil pipeline tariffs.
newsitem.headline: Russia energy body sets new oil pipeline tariffs.

text.p: Russia's Federal Energy Commission has approved new crude oil pipeline tariffs, some higher, some lower, in line with a recent government decree.
The tariffs, which come into effect on October 21, range from 15 roubles to 37.1 roubles per tonne per km, the official Itar-Tass news agency said.
Oil shipments along the Druzhba (Friendship) pipeline through Ukraine to eastern Europe carry the lowest tariff.
The duties follow a July government decree calling for duties charged by natural monopolies to be regulated in the second half of this year.
Interfax news agency said four oil pipelines would carry higher tariffs. It did not give comparisons for all rates.

Users of the Urals-Siberian pipeline would now pay a higher 15 roubles per tonne per km. Shipments through through the Volga region would carry a 15.26 rouble duty, while supplies through links in northwestern Russia would cost 15.1 roubles.
Deliveries through the Upper Volga system would increase six percent to 15.8 roubles.
Rates would fall to 37.10 roubles from 40.76 roubles for shipments through the Northern Links Pipelines, to 25.8 roubles for Trans-Siberian pipelines and to 15 roubles for Druzhba.
Transneft, the oil transport monopoly, is obliged to stick to these tariffs. Producers have criticised Transneft for charging what they say are higher than justified rates. ($1 = 5,426 roubles)
